summary: Containers are the recommended environment for ansible-test because they are consistent, and unit tests run network-isolated. --docker uses Docker or Podman, preferring Docker unless ANSIBLE_TEST_PREFER_PODMAN is set.
questions: How do I make ansible-test use Podman instead of Docker?
Why should I run ansible-test in a container?
Do unit tests have network access under --docker?
What does the --docker flag do in ansible-test?

answer_card.title: Run ansible-test in containers
answer_card.answer_md:
Use `--docker` to run tests in a container (works with Docker or Podman). Containers give a consistent environment, and unit tests run with no network access.

If both engines are installed, Docker wins. To force Podman:
```shell
export ANSIBLE_TEST_PREFER_PODMAN=1
```
